stories.title: PROLA adapts weather models for high-resolution forecasting via low-rank tuning
stories.summary: Researchers propose PROLA, a Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation method for adapting pretrained weather models to predict high-resolution future conditions from coarse current data.
stories.more: The paper frames this as Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling, refining both spatial and temporal resolution while forecasting future states. It aims to make adapting large pretrained weather backbones for local forecasts less costly. The approach builds on existing large pretrained weather models rather than training new ones from scratch. The paper's full benchmark results were not included in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Game2Player co-develops games and AI players to scale gameplay training data
stories.summary: Game2Player is a framework that jointly develops game environments and AI players to collect diverse, verifiable gameplay experience at scale for training visual agents.
stories.more: The authors note that collecting human gameplay data is costly, and learning from existing gameplay videos requires inferring actions that were not recorded. Existing gameplay datasets also cover a limited range of games and often lack explicit tasks or verifiable outcomes. Game2Player aims to address both gaps by generating environments and players together. The excerpt did not specify which games or benchmarks were used to evaluate the framework.

stories.title: Paper argues noisy evaluation, not weak proposals, stalls AI agent self-improvement
stories.summary: Researchers propose the 'Resolution Hypothesis': agent self-improvement loops often fail not because proposed changes are bad, but because noisy evaluation can't reliably tell better artifacts from worse ones.
stories.more: Agent evolution loops typically have a proposer generate candidate prompts, skills, or memories, with a selection step accepting higher-scoring ones. The paper notes that methods often trade wins inconsistently across studies, and evolution sometimes fails to bootstrap at all on certain tasks. The authors trace this puzzle to evaluation noise rather than proposal quality. The excerpt did not specify what fix the paper proposes for improving evaluation reliability.

stories.title: ALIVE makes streaming video models proactive and interactive
stories.summary: ALIVE is an interactive streaming video model that supports proactive monitoring, coordinating streaming tasks, and seeking feedback from users rather than only responding to isolated requests.
stories.more: The authors built two new datasets, ALIVE-SFT-288K and ALIVE-RL-3K, for a two-stage training process. Supervised fine-tuning teaches the model when and how to respond, while reinforcement learning with a method called Behavior-Aligned Credit Assignment combines trajectory-level and local signals. The goal is to let streaming video LLMs engage more naturally during continuous observation rather than treating each request in isolation. The excerpt did not include evaluation results against other streaming video models.

stories.title: VideoNexus proposes delegating video perception to ease reasoning-context load
stories.summary: VideoNexus is a new approach for long-video understanding that delegates visual perception to a separate module, aiming to avoid overloading a reasoning model's context with accumulated visual detail.
stories.more: The paper notes that existing video agents can inspect footage selectively but still accumulate visual information in the planner's reasoning context over time. Delegating perception is meant to ease that burden, though sparse sampling risks missing important details. The approach targets long, dense video sequences where both perception and reasoning are heavily taxed. The excerpt did not include quantitative results comparing VideoNexus to prior approaches.

stories.title: Paper proposes an Environment Evolution Loop to scale long-horizon coding agents
stories.summary: Researchers introduce a method for converting code repositories into training environments with an evolving feedback loop, aimed at improving long-horizon coding agent training.
stories.more: The paper notes existing pipelines often follow a linear process ending in validation, which establishes usability but offers little guidance on improving training value over time. Recursive self-improvement approaches typically require costly model rollouts or training followed by downstream evaluation, with feedback delays that worsen on long-horizon tasks. The proposed Environment Evolution Loop aims to use timelier, more reliable proxy signals instead. The excerpt did not detail the specific proxy signals used or report benchmark results.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon, a frontier model for coding and science
stories.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, a frontier model for software development, science, and knowledge work that handles text, images, video, audio, and PDFs with a million-token context window.
stories.more: Neon is Google's fourth new Gemini model released within a month, following Hydrogen, Argon, and Carbon. It is priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, higher than earlier Gemini 4 models. An early independent write-up argued Neon performs comparably to Anthropic's Opus 5.5 on certain tasks, drawing significant discussion on Hacker News. Google has not detailed Neon's exact training approach or full benchmark results.

stories.summary: Internal chats show Meta staff are concerned about its Muse AI producing erratic outputs that appear to share people's bank and bitcoin balances, though Meta says the figures are not real.
stories.more: Meta maintains that the shared financial figures are fabricated rather than genuine leaked data. Despite that assurance, internal staff chats reportedly show ongoing alarm over the behavior. The excerpt did not specify what has caused Muse to generate this type of erratic output.

items.excerpt: Erratic Muse outputs sharing random bank, bitcoin balances aren’t real, Meta says.

stories.title: Will Wright's new simulation game will use AI to mine players' personal memories
stories.summary: Sims creator Will Wright is developing a new simulation project called MyMems that uses AI to pull content from players' own memories, aiming to 'turn the simulation inward.'
stories.more: Wright described the goal as shifting simulation games to draw on personal, real-life material rather than purely fictional scenarios. The excerpt did not detail how the AI mining process works or when the project will be available.

stories.summary: Google introduced temporary threads for AI Mode in Search, letting users have conversations without adding them to search history or influencing future recommendations.
stories.more: The new temporary threads work similarly to other incognito browsing features, keeping AI Mode conversations out of a user's permanent history. The excerpt did not specify how to activate the feature or whether it is available to all users yet.

stories.summary: Satya Nadella said AI agents could disrupt advertising-driven business models online, forcing companies like Amazon to rethink how they compete for customers.

He singled out Amazon as a company that may need to adapt its competitive strategy. The excerpt did not report a timeline for when Nadella expects this shift to occur.

stories.title: OpenAI says its models improved AMD's GPU chip design by about a year's progress
stories.summary: OpenAI said that, working with AMD, its models delivered up to a 14% PPA improvement on AMD's flagship GPU IP in under five months, which it estimates as roughly a year's worth of typical progress.
stories.more: AMD has already folded the changes into a chip design that has moved to production. OpenAI published the results in its own post on chip design, which was also submitted to Hacker News. The Decoder noted Anthropic is pursuing similar work, applying AI to chip design to optimize cost and performance per dollar. Neither company detailed which specific chip or node is affected by the AMD collaboration.
